title: Token Cost Allocation Tracking
summary: Attribute inference usage to the business work that caused it, including retries, caches, tools, and shared infrastructure.
overview: Token cost allocation maps model usage to a tenant, team, workflow, or product feature. It requires more than multiplying a final response’s token count by a price: retries, planning calls, embedding requests, cache reads or writes, multimodal inputs, and failed attempts can all contribute. Self-hosted inference also needs infrastructure cost allocation rather than provider token billing alone.

The accounting system should distinguish estimated usage at admission from observed usage and reconciled billing. Prices and billing categories vary by provider, model, region, and contract, so a versioned rate catalog is essential. Allocation is an operational and financial measurement system; it should not expose sensitive prompt contents merely to identify ownership.

production.poc: A prototype tags every model call with a workflow and feature identifier and compares estimates with returned usage.
production.production: Production records attempt-level usage, rate versions, cache categories, and unattributed cost exceptions.
production.scale: Enterprise scale reconciles invoices, allocates shared capacity with documented rules, and connects budgets to admission without silently blocking essential workflows.

components.name: Usage envelope
components.role: Carries tenant, feature, workflow, and attempt identifiers through inference calls.

components.name: Provider usage adapter
components.role: Normalizes model-specific reported usage while preserving original categories.

components.name: Rate catalog
components.role: Stores effective prices and contractual dimensions by date and model.

components.name: Cost ledger
components.role: Records immutable estimated, observed, and reconciled amounts.

components.name: Budget and reporting service
components.role: Aggregates ownership and informs quotas, alerts, and capacity decisions.

flow.title: Assign ownership
flow.description: Attach a stable cost center and workflow identity before any model or embedding call.

flow.title: Estimate admission cost
flow.description: Use input size and output limits to reserve an approximate budget.

flow.title: Record every attempt
flow.description: Capture provider, model, usage categories, cache behavior, and retry relationships.

flow.title: Apply versioned rates
flow.description: Calculate observed cost using the rate effective for the actual usage event.

flow.title: Reconcile totals
flow.description: Compare the ledger with provider billing or infrastructure allocation and investigate differences.

flow.title: Report accepted-task economics
flow.description: Include failures and retries when comparing routes or product features.

useCase.title: Allocating assistant spend across product features
useCase.situation: A collaboration platform offers document summaries, meeting follow-ups, and workspace search to several business units.
useCase.problem: Shared provider invoices cannot explain which features generate retries or expensive long-context work.
useCase.requirement: Attribute complete accepted-task cost without logging private document text.
useCase.architecture: Usage envelopes connect every inference attempt to feature and business-unit identifiers, and a ledger applies effective rates.
runtime: A summary task records its planner, generation, and retry calls under one workflow.
Reports compare total cost with accepted results and reconcile unexplained provider charges.
useCase.failure: If a provider omits final usage after a broken stream, the ledger retains an estimate and marks it pending reconciliation.
useCase.impact: Measure unattributed spend, reconciliation variance, and cost per accepted task; a low reported average is misleading when failed attempts are excluded.

tradeoffs.cost: Increases event volume and ownership metadata management.
Differ from actual generation and billing.
Requires an agreed rule for idle and reserved capacity.

failures.scenario: Retry cost is double-counted or omitted
failures.detection: Ledger totals diverge from attempt records.
failures.recovery: Use unique usage-event IDs and explicit retry relationships.
Apply effective-dated rates and immutable reconciled entries.

mistakes.fix: Include all attempts and supporting model work.
Use a versioned provider and contract rate catalog.

mistakes.mistake: Equating tokens with all infrastructure cost
mistakes.fix: Account for idle, storage, network, and accelerator allocation where relevant.

whenToUse: Use for multi-tenant products and shared AI platforms.
Use when routing and caching decisions need economic evidence.
Use for budget alerts and documented chargeback.
whenNotToUse: Avoid exposing raw prompts in accounting records.
Do not treat estimates as final invoices.
Avoid cost comparisons that ignore task acceptance quality.
checklist: Report cost per accepted task including retries.
